preconditions.description: Attacker must be contract owner to set operationsAddress via setOperationsAddress()
Contract must have accumulated tokensForOperations > 0 to trigger swapBack() execution
Contract balance must be >= swapTokensAtAmount to enable swapBack

logic_check.expected_value: 0 after swapBack should empty contract ETH balance

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. As owner, call setOperationsAddress() with a contract that rejects ETH transfers (no receive/fallback payable function). 2. Trigger token transfers that accumulate fees until tokensForOperations > 0 and contract token balance >= swapTokensAtAmount. 3. This triggers swapBack() which attempts to send ETH to operationsAddress via unchecked .call{value: ...}. 4. The transfer fails silently (success=false not checked), ETH remains stuck in contract, but tokensForOperations is reset to 0. 5. Contract state becomes inconsistent - fees collected but never distributed.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is an Unchecked Transfer in the swapBack() function. The line `(success,) = address(operationsAddress).call{value: address(this).balance}(""` declares a success variable but never checks it. If the ETH transfer fails (e.g., operationsAddress rejects ETH), the transaction continues without reverting, but ETH remains stuck in the contract. The oracle expects address(this).balance to be 0 after swapBack, but it won't be if the transfer fails.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious contract without payable receive/fallback to reject ETH. 2. Impersonate the owner to set operationsAddress to the malicious contract. 3. Enable trading. 4. Trigger token transfers that accumulate fees and trigger swapBack(). 5. The ETH transfer to operationsAddress will fail silently, leaving ETH stuck in the contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy MaliciousContract without payable receive/fallback. 2. Impersonate owner via vm.prank(). 3. Call setOperationsAddress() with malicious contract. 4. Call enableTrading(). 5. Transfer tokens to LP pair to trigger fee accumulation and swapBack(). 6. Verify ETH is stuck (balance > 0).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract balance is 0 because the swapTokensForEth() call on the DEX router returned 0 ETH (no liquidity in the pair). The tokensForOperations counter wasn't reset because swapBack() returned early when ethBalance was 0. Need to add liquidity to enable the swap, then the ETH transfer to malicious contract will fail.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Add liquidity to the LP pair (tokens + ETH) so swaps can work. 2. Transfer tokens to accumulate fees in the contract. 3. Trigger swapBack() which will generate ETH from the swap. 4. The ETH transfer to malicious contract will fail silently, leaving ETH stuck.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner and add liquidity to LP pair. 2. Transfer tokens to trigger fee accumulation. 3. Call forceSwapBack() to trigger the vulnerable code path. 4. Verify ETH is stuck in contract.
attempts.failure_reflection: The swapBack() didn't execute properly because: 1) The LP pair has no liquidity so the token->ETH swap returns 0 ETH, 2) tokensForOperations wasn't reset because swapBack returned early. Need to add liquidity to the LP pair first and ensure the swap generates actual ETH before the failed transfer.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The order of operations was wrong. Trading must be enabled before any token transfers can occur (unless excluded from fees). The attacker needs to transfer tokens to add liquidity, but trading wasn't active yet.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner and enable trading FIRST. 2. Transfer tokens to attacker. 3. Add liquidity to LP pair. 4. Set malicious operations address. 5. Transfer tokens to LP pair to accumulate fees. 6. Force swapBack to trigger the vulnerable ETH transfer.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner, enable trading. 2. Transfer tokens to attacker. 3. Add liquidity (tokens + ETH) to enable swaps. 4. Set malicious operations address. 5. Transfer tokens to LP pair to trigger fee accumulation. 6. Force swapBack and verify ETH is stuck.
attempts.failure_reflection: The error occurs because trading is not active when trying to add liquidity. The token's _transfer function requires trading to be active OR sender/recipient to be excluded from fees. The owner is excluded, but the attacker is not. Need to enable trading BEFORE adding liquidity.
